prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Boundary: receiving to outbound release. Elements/aliases: Inbound Inspection Desk=Cinderbay (checks paperwork, trailer ID/seals, damage; records outcomes before routine handling; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note to Yard Gate Controller). Pallet Dimension Scanner=Moonquarry (produces Oversize Load Advisory, not placement authorization; identifies alternate handling path). Inbound Pallet Buffer (controlled staging). North Aisle Stacker Crane=Juniperwake (sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot); South Aisle Stacker Crane; both report availability. East/West Transfer Conveyors (separate routes). Conveyor Line Controller=Brasshaven (produces Transfer Induction Ticket; stops equipment on downstream blocks). Autonomous Forklift Fleet=Larkspur (produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation: vehicle, pallet, time, deferred moves). Yard Gate Controller=Velvetrook (validates arrivals, flags unscheduled, assigns doors; records discrepancies, holds risky vehicles). Outbound Dispatch Sorter (receives Dispatch Wave Amendment). Outbound Checkweigh Scale (weight before record finalized). Shipping Documentation Desk. Safety Zone Controller, Fire Alarm Panel (Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice; safety status stops movement). Maintenance Release Terminal=Copperfield (produces Crane Service Release Card after checks). Warehouse Management System=Morrowglass (authoritative state; releases work, plans waves; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; reconciles tasks/constraints). Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (sees exceptions until resolved; defers work; reviews delays, stops, constraints before next wave); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel. Requirements: valid receipt; window checked; seals/ID before unloading; damaged pallets segregated; unsafe issues pause unloading; restricted pallets in approved positions; cranes authorized zones; conveyor entry after inspection; interlocks; blocked points hold upstream; single merges; duplicate inductions held; stale status holds; post-fault order preserved; no work without WMS release; sorter keeps order unless amended, verifies staging; forklifts need valid status/route/destination, prioritize by priority/battery/proximity, confirm pallet before lift, limit speed, stop on safety blocks; requests need unique reference, destination, constraints; maintenance authorization recorded before return to service; attribute mismatch blocks auto allocation, traceable hold, record retains scan, location, time.

Document units:
S151: Cinderbay consumes its inspection-stage advisory and records whether the pallet can proceed, requires rework, or must remain held.
S152: A held pallet remains separated from available stock until the review outcome is entered and validated.
S153: Inbound Pallet Buffer provides temporary staging without implying that a held load has been accepted into inventory.
S154: North Aisle Stacker Crane uses the Slot Reservation Receipt to confirm that its assigned destination remains reserved.
S155: Before movement, the crane checks its current task state and stops if the destination or access path is no longer valid.
S156: Morrowglass, the Warehouse Management System, consumes the load advisory to apply the required handling constraints to affected work.
S157: The system prevents an incompatible allocation from being released while the advisory remains applicable.
S158: If a task is blocked, the control record identifies the hold reason and retains the pallet's last confirmed location.
S159: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews unresolved holds and assigns an escalation when the operating team cannot clear them locally.
S160: The supervisor also confirms that a delayed task will not compromise a later outbound wave or an aisle access limit.
S161: Service readiness requires a recorded fault state, a controlled work area, and a clear separation between maintenance activity and live movement.
S162: North Aisle Stacker Crane reports a fault that could affect positioning, load retention, braking, or travel before the equipment is returned to service.
S163: The affected crane remains unavailable while personnel inspect the fault and verify that adjacent equipment can continue safely.
S164: Maintenance Release Terminal records the inspection outcome and the identity of the person authorizing a return to operation.
S165: A failed test keeps the equipment inhibited and returns the fault to the maintenance queue for further diagnosis.
S166: A successful test does not by itself release the crane until required interlocks and operating limits have been checked.
S167: Outbound Checkweigh Scale produces the Gross Weight Variance Slip when a measured pallet weight falls outside the configured tolerance.
S168: The variance remains unresolved until the pallet is reweighed or the documented review establishes a safe disposition.
S169: Conveyor Line Controller holds affected transfers when an exception would make the next movement uncertain.
S170: Fire Alarm Panel and Safety Zone Controller retain authority to stop or restrict movement whenever their safety status requires it.
S171: Warehouse Operations Supervisor releases normal work only after outstanding exceptions, maintenance holds, and access constraints have been reconciled.
